answer: Slashable collateral escrow curbs Sybil attacks by requiring each agent key to lock scarce tokens in a smart contract across an unbonding window. Verifiers submit fraud proofs to burn deposits if a key double-signs conflicting messages. Like a stone terrace shielding a meadow from runoff, per-key bonds keep fake swarms from draining protocol nectar by imposing linear liquidity costs per identity. Still, wealthy attackers can fund many keys while low-capital builders get priced out.
